trees.title: A gear problem
trees.summary: It's hard to change gear, the clutch is slipping, or the automatic gearbox is behaving oddly.
trees.safety: If the car doesn't move at all when you shift to D or R, or the gearbox responds with sharp, unusual jolts — drive with maximum care straight to a garage, and don't keep trying again and again.

n1.q: What type of gearbox does the car have?

n2.q: What's happening with the manual gearbox?

options.label: It's hard to get into gear, or you hear a clunk when shifting
Engine RPM rises under acceleration, but road speed doesn't rise at the same rate
The gear “pops” out by itself while driving
A hum that changes with the gear selected

n3.q: Does the difficulty getting into gear happen even when the clutch pedal is pressed all the way down?

options.label: Yes, even when the clutch is pressed all the way down
Only when the clutch isn't pressed all the way down

n5.q: What's happening with the automatic gearbox?

options.label: Gear changes feel like a kick or a sharp jolt
The car doesn't move at all when you shift to D or R, but the engine responds fine at idle
A “limited limp mode” warning light (a wrench or turtle symbol) comes on the dashboard
The gear lever is stuck and won't move out of P

r-clutch-slip.text: When engine RPM rises but road speed doesn't rise at the same rate, mainly on a hill or under strong acceleration, the clutch isn't transferring all the power — probably because the clutch disc is worn.
actions: Go to a garage; a slipping clutch will only get worse.
Avoid towing or heavy loads until it's checked.

r-gear-pops-out.result: Suspected worn gear lock in the manual gearbox
r-gear-pops-out.text: A gear that pops out by itself while driving, mainly under acceleration or going downhill, points to wear in the gear-locking mechanism inside the gearbox.
actions: Hold the gear lever lightly when this happens, to identify which gear it recurs in.
Go to a garage; this isn't a fault that goes away on its own.

r-gearbox-bearing.result: Suspected worn bearing inside the gearbox
r-gearbox-bearing.text: A hum that changes with the gear selected, and not just with road speed, points to an internal bearing in the gearbox starting to wear.
actions: Go to a garage for a check; the longer you wait, the more the repair may grow.
Avoid long drives until it's checked.

r-clutch-not-disengaging.text: Difficulty getting into gear even when the clutch is pressed all the way down means the clutch isn't disconnecting the engine from the gearbox properly — a problem with the cable, the hydraulic clutch cylinder, or the disc itself.
actions: Go to a garage; continuing to drive like this wears the gearbox's synchros.

r-clutch-adjustment-ok.result: A foot habit with the clutch pedal — not a fault
r-clutch-adjustment-ok.text: Difficulty getting into gear only when the clutch isn't pressed fully down is expected — the gearbox needs full disengagement to shift smoothly.
actions: Get into the habit of pressing the clutch pedal all the way down on every gear change.

r-auto-harsh-shift.result: Suspected problem in the automatic gearbox or its fluid
r-auto-harsh-shift.text: Sharp shifts or kicks between gears in an automatic gearbox, that weren't there before, point to dirty transmission fluid, an incorrect fluid level, or the start of a problem in the shifting mechanism.
actions: Check the level and condition of the transmission fluid according to the owner's manual, if there's a dipstick.
Go to a garage; waiting can turn a simple repair into an expensive one.

r-auto-no-drive.result: The car doesn't move — suspected failure in the automatic gearbox
r-auto-no-drive.text: When the engine responds normally at idle but the car doesn't move at all when you shift to D or R, there's a suspected serious problem in the gearbox or its link to the engine.
actions: Don't keep trying again and again — this can make the damage worse.
Call for a tow to a garage; there's no roadside fix for this.

r-limp-mode.result: The car has switched to limp mode
r-limp-mode.text: When the car's computer detects a serious fault in the gearbox or the engine, it limits acceleration and the number of available gears to prevent further damage — this is deliberate, not an additional fault in itself.
actions: Drive carefully, at low speed, straight to the nearest garage.
Don't keep switching the car off and on again to “try to reset it” without knowing what caused it.

r-shifter-lock.result: A safety lock on the gear lever
r-shifter-lock.text: In most automatic cars the gear lever is locked in P until the brake pedal is pressed — a protection against moving it by mistake.
actions: Press the brake pedal all the way down while you move the lever.
If it's still stuck even with the brake pressed, there's usually a hidden key-release lock near the lever; follow the owner's manual.
